title: Minimum Operations to Make Binary Array Elements Equal to One I
summary: Given a binary array, you can flip any three consecutive elements any number of times.
statement: Given a binary array, you can flip any three consecutive elements any number of times. Determine the minimum operations needed to make all elements equal to 1, or return -1 if impossible.
constraints: nums is a nonempty binary array.
One operation flips exactly three consecutive elements.
Return the minimum operations that make every element one, or -1 when impossible.
hints: Once the scan passes index i, no later length-three flip can change it.
Therefore flip at i exactly when its current value is zero, then verify the final two bits.
Scan i=0..n-3; if nums[i]==0 flip i..i+2 and increment; return count if all ones else -1.
The leftmost unresolved bit forces every greedy decision, establishing both necessity and minimality.
editorial: The leftmost unresolved bit forces every greedy decision, establishing both necessity and minimality.

tests.explanation: Greedily flipping at indices zero, one, and three produces all ones in three operations.
No length-three operation exists, so this array cannot be completed.
